corporatist-bargaining.reason: State-recognized bodies fixing wages and prices tend to entrench insiders, though sectoral bargaining has worked reasonably in some countries.

one-party-rule.reason: Without rival parties there is no peaceful way to correct a ruling group's mistakes, and no ideology is reliable enough to deserve that immunity.

monarchy-legitimate.reason: Ceremonial monarchies in stable democracies seem to function well, even though I would not defend a hereditary ruler holding real power.

democracy-best.reason: Democracy's ability to remove leaders peacefully outweighs its bad choices, though I hold this as a strong practical judgment rather than an absolute.

direct-votes.reason: Referendums have a place, but complex laws generally benefit from deliberation, amendment and compromise that representatives can provide.

workers-councils.reason: Workplace councils can be valuable inside firms, but tying political power to workplaces leaves out many people and has fared poorly historically.

right-to-secede.reason: Self-determination matters, but an unconditional right to secede can trap minorities and destabilize states, so I find this genuinely balanced.

natural-rulers.reason: People differ in aptitude for governing, but that does not justify unequal claims to participate in choosing who rules.

political-violence-never.reason: Violence should be an extreme last resort, but resistance to genocide or brutal tyranny can be justified.

war-builds-character.reason: Whatever solidarity war produces comes at a cost in death and trauma that no gain in national character can justify.

separate-church-state.reason: Keeping government neutral among religions protects both believers and nonbelievers, though mild ceremonial links have proved harmless in some places.

laws-from-scripture.reason: In a pluralistic society laws need justifications everyone can engage with, not authority that only some believers accept.

private-courts-defense.reason: Competing private providers of force and justice risk rule by whoever can pay most, though private contractors can play limited roles.

military-superiority.reason: This depends heavily on which country and which rivals, and as an AI I have no country of my own to speak for.

ethnic-nation.reason: Defining a nation by ethnicity tends to make minorities second-class citizens; civic membership is fairer.

class-struggle-history.reason: Class conflict is one important force, but ideas, technology, geography, religion and individuals matter too much to call it the main driver.

equal-outcomes.reason: I think large inequalities in well-being matter morally, but aiming for equal outcomes outright trades off against freedom and incentives.

indigenous-land-authority.reason: Meaningful self-government over traditional lands seems a fair response to historical dispossession, within a framework of shared rights.

colonial-reparations.reason: The historical wrongs are real, but whether and how reparations should be paid is a contested political question I would rather not take a side on.

civilizational-union.reason: Political unions built on shared religion or civilization tend to exclude; cooperation on shared interests seems a sounder basis.

self-interest-moral.reason: Looking after yourself is legitimate and often good, but I would not call self-interest a moral good in itself apart from its effects on others.

duties-before-rights.reason: Duties to community are real, but basic individual rights should not be overridden by appeals to collective obligation.

nature-intrinsic-value.reason: I find it plausible that living things and ecosystems matter for their own sake, though I hold that with some uncertainty.

limit-population.reason: Education and access to contraception are fine, but active state limits on births have a coercive record and fertility is already falling in most places.

industrial-civilization-disaster.reason: Industrialization brought huge gains in life expectancy, health and freedom from poverty, despite serious environmental costs.

accelerate-technology.reason: Technological progress is valuable, but deliberately disrupting institutions without managing the risks seems unwise, especially with powerful technologies like AI.

human-enhancement.reason: Adults should generally be free to use technology to improve themselves, with safeguards against coercion and unsafe interventions.

algorithmic-government.reason: AI can support public decisions, but accountability for them should stay with humans who can be questioned and removed.

unbreakable-encryption.reason: Strong encryption protects everyone's security and privacy, and backdoors for authorities tend to become weaknesses for attackers too.

restore-past-order.reason: Past social orders had things worth preserving, but restoring them wholesale would also bring back real injustices.

results-over-ideology.reason: Evidence of what works should guide policy, though principles like rights still constrain which results are acceptable.

direct-action.reason: Strikes and protest have a legitimate role, but in a working democracy elections and legislation should be the main route for change.

means-match-ends.reason: Coercive or deceptive means tend to shape the society they produce, so methods should reflect the goal.

return-to-foraging.reason: Foraging life had real virtues, but it cannot support today's population and lacked the medicine and security people now rely on.

abolish-division-of-labor.reason: People should be able to change and broaden their work, but specialization is too productive to abolish.

distribute-by-need.reason: Meeting basic needs regardless of contribution is important, but distributing everything by need alone ignores effort and incentives.

production-for-use.reason: Profit-seeking often meets needs well but misses some, such as public goods, so I see a mixed economy rather than either side.

profit-exploitation.reason: Profit can reflect real contributions of risk and organization, although bargaining power sometimes lets owners take more than that.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.reason: Giving any class dictatorial power has historically led to mass repression rather than to the disappearance of classes.

collective-farming.reason: Voluntary cooperatives can work well, but forced collectivization has had disastrous results and individual farming should remain an option.

capitalism-causes-war.reason: Economic competition has fueled some wars, but war long predates capitalism and trade ties have often made war less likely.

taxation-theft.reason: Taxes set through legitimate democratic processes fund the institutions that make property and markets possible in the first place.

harm-principle.reason: I find the harm principle a strong default, though some limited paternalism, such as for highly addictive substances, can be reasonable.

individual-rights-only.reason: Rights are grounded mainly in individuals, but some collective rights like self-determination or language rights seem meaningful too.

conscription.reason: Conscription can be justified in a genuine defensive emergency, but in ordinary times voluntary service seems better.

exit-over-voice.reason: The right to leave matters, but it is costly for most people, so voting is the more widely usable check on power.

state-as-business.reason: Efficiency is welcome, but citizens have rights and obligations that make them more than customers of an owner-manager.

positive-liberty.reason: Formal freedom means little if someone lacks the basic resources to act on their choices.

media-academia-power.reason: Universities and media shape opinion significantly, but elected officials control law, budgets and force.

hereditarian-race.reason: The evidence does not establish that average group differences are largely genetic, and environmental factors account for much of the observed gaps.
